dicas.texto: Você está indo muito bem! Quando temos retas com divisões diferentes, o que acontece com o tamanho de cada 'pedaço' quando aumentamos o número de divisões?
Tente marcar o ponto 4/7 na segunda reta. Depois de marcar os dois pontos, observe a distância de cada um em relação ao zero (o início da reta).
Compare a posição visual dos pontos. O ponto 2/3 está mais próximo do 1 ou mais próximo do 0 do que o ponto 4/7?
Olhe para a reta: 2/3 é o mesmo que 14/21 e 4/7 é o mesmo que 12/21. Qual desses valores ocupa um espaço maior na reta numérica?

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma para cada quantidade (rotuladas "Amount Kewana painted" e "Amount Adam painted"); para cada reta há um campo onde o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividi-la (com confirmação) e, depois, marca o ponto da fração correspondente; abaixo, um seletor em que o aluno escolhe UMA destas alternativas: "Kewana painted more fence."; "Adam painted more fence."; "Both painted same amount of fence."; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir cada reta, marcar cada ponto, escolher a alternativa, concluir).

Mark Kewana's point at 2/3 on the divided number line.
Divide Adam's number line into equal parts and enter the number of parts.
Mark Adam's point at 4/7 on the divided number line.
Use the two marked points to choose who painted more fence.
Press Done to record the completed comparison for 2/3.

erros.devolutiva: The numerator tells how many intervals to count, while the denominator tells how many equal intervals make the whole. Keep 2 on top and 3 below.
erros.buggyRule: Posicionar o ponto invertendo numerador e denominador (ex: 3/2 em vez de 2/3)

erros.devolutiva: Adam's number line represents only Adam's fraction. Use his denominator, 7, rather than adding both denominators.
erros.buggyRule: Somar os dois denominadores para criar uma escala única: {A_den} + {B_den}

erros.devolutiva: A single interval shows only the whole. Adam's fraction needs the whole divided into smaller equal parts.
erros.buggyRule: Marcar apenas 1 divisão (o inteiro) ignorando o denominador

erros.devolutiva: Count the spaces between the marks, not the marks themselves. The target is four intervals out of seven.
erros.buggyRule: Contar as marcas de divisão como se fossem o ponto da fração (contar marcas em vez de intervalos)

erros.devolutiva: Do not switch the numerator and denominator. Count four intervals on a line divided into seven equal parts.
erros.buggyRule: Posicionar o ponto invertendo numerador e denominador (ex: 3/2 em vez de 2/3)

erros.devolutiva: You compared only the numerators and chose 4 because it is greater than 2. The denominator also determines the size of each part.
erros.buggyRule: Escolher a fração com o maior numerador como sendo a maior

erros.valor: Both painted same amount of fence.
erros.devolutiva: The two fractions do not occupy the same position. Compare the actual locations of 2/3 and 4/7 on the number lines.
erros.buggyRule: Comparar pela diferença para o inteiro (gap thinking): quanto menor a diferença para o inteiro, maior a fração

dicas.texto: What does the denominator tell you about the number line?
Look at the denominator in Kewana's fraction and use it as the number of equal intervals from 0 to 1.
Kewana's fraction is 2/3, so focus on the number 3 below the fraction bar.
Enter the denominator as the number of equal parts, then confirm the division.
Which number tells you how many equal parts to count from zero?
Begin at 0 and count intervals toward 1, using the numerator as the number of intervals.
Count two intervals from 0 on Kewana's line.
Click the second division point on the line divided into three equal intervals.
What does the denominator represent when you divide a number line?
Find Adam's denominator and use it to set the number of equal intervals from 0 to 1.
Adam's fraction is 4/7, so use the number below the fraction bar.
Enter the denominator as the number of equal parts, then confirm Adam's number line.
Which part of the fraction tells you how far to move from zero?
Start at 0 and count the required number of intervals toward 1.
Count four intervals on Adam's line, which has seven equal intervals in total.
Click the fourth division point on the line divided into seven equal intervals.
On a number line from 0 to 1, which fraction is greater: the point farther left or the point farther right?
Compare the locations of the two marked points rather than comparing only their numerators.
Look carefully at which marked point is closer to 1.
Select the student whose marked point lies farther to the right on the number line.
What fraction represents Kewana's painted amount?
Check that both points were marked between 0 and 1 and that the comparison choice is selected.
Make sure the selected comparison agrees with the point that is farther to the right.
After checking the selected comparison, press the Done button to register the conclusion.

exercicio.statement:
Kewana and Adam are earning money by painting both sides of a fence. When it was lunch time, they decided to compare who has painted more since they started. Use the number line to find out which student has painted more of the fence.
Kewana has painted 2/3 of one side of the fence.
Adam has painted 4/7 of the other side of the fence.
Who has painted more fence?

steps.instruction: Divide Kewana's number line into equal parts and enter the number of parts.
Mark Kewana's point at 2/3 on the divided number line.
Divide Adam's number line into equal parts and enter the number of parts.
Mark Adam's point at 4/7 on the divided number line.
Use the two marked points to choose who painted more fence.
Press Done to record the completed comparison for 2/3.
